newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on storage tickets, funds.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on storage tickets, funds.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended lower on a continued selloff of 90-day storage certificates, hedges and fund selling, traders said.

"We had some more 90-day pricing, local, commercial and fund selling with scale-down crusher buying," a trader said. Jan-Mar spread at $2.20, Sep-Nov $3.50, Jan-May $3.30. January futures crush margin rose to -34.82 from -36.19 Friday. Volume was 3,437 lots, or 68,740 tonnes, with 375 hedges.
January canola fell $3.90 to $398.10. January flax fell $2.30 to $354.70 on hedges, 90-day storage certificate sales and Cargill was a scale-down buyer. Jan-Mar spread at $4.
March feed wheat lost $0.40 to $168.50 and May fell $1 to $166.50 on commission sales to realign spreads while commercials bought.

Barley set new contract lows in all but the October contract. February western barley closed $1.40 lower at $135.10, its new contract low and March slipped $1.60 to $134.50, also its new low, on commission house selling and lower CBOT feed grain values.
Oats and feed peas did not trade.
(Values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats).
